headline: City Council Emergency Session Called Over 'Unregulated Meme Activity'
subheadline: Proposed ordinance would require meme permits for posts with over 100 likes
summary: Local officials are debating new regulations on social media content creation following complaints about 'excessive irony' in the downtown area.
content:
An emergency session of the City Council was convened Tuesday evening after residents of the Riverside District filed a formal complaint about what they called "a dangerous proliferation of unregulated meme activity."

The complaint, signed by 47 residents, cited concerns about "sarcasm pollution," "irony runoff," and the potential for "catastrophic context collapse" if meme production continues unchecked.

"We've seen a 340% increase in people saying things they don't mean," explained Councilwoman Patricia Hayes, presenting a slideshow that appeared to contain several examples of the very memes in question. "The youth are communicating entirely in references we don't understand."

The proposed Meme Licensing and Irony Regulation Act (MLIRA) would require content creators to obtain a permit for any post receiving more than 100 likes. Creators would need to pass a written exam on "proper context usage" and "responsible sarcasm deployment."

Local college student and prolific meme creator @ChaoticNeutral_Steve spoke against the measure. "They literally cannot stop us," he said. "We are chaos. We are everywhere." He then posted a picture of the council members with the caption "this meeting could have been an email."

The council will vote on the measure next month, assuming they can figure out how to use the new voting software.
author: Tom Hendricks, City Hall Reporter
